transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, it's really hard for me to talk about, but since my divorce I've been eating huge meals by myself late at night. I end up doing it alone because I'm just so embarrassed by how much I eat around other people.
During these late-night eating episodes, do you feel like you're unable to stop eating or control how much you're eating, even if you want to?

Yes, absolutely. Once I start, it's like a switch flips and I just can't stop. Even while I'm telling myself "Santiago, stop, this is crazy," my hands just keep going back to the food like they aren't listening to me.
Do you often feel guilty or ashamed after these episodes of eating large amounts of food, and do you try to hide evidence of what you've eaten from others?

Yes, I feel deeply ashamed and embarrassed by how much I eat. I try to hide it by barely eating anything when I'm around my family or soccer friends, and then I wait until I'm locked inside my apartment alone so no one can see what I'm doing.

How often do you experience these episodes of eating large amounts of food in a short period of time, and do you also restrict your food intake or engage in excessive exercise to compensate for the calories consumed during these episodes?

This has been happening at least a few nights every week for most of this past year. I don't do any excessive exercise to make up for it, but I do skip lunch at work and turn down dinners with my teammates so I can "save up" for the late-night eating.

The patient's behavior of restricting food intake during the day to 'save up' for late-night eating also aligns with F50.2. Therefore, the current candidate is F50.2.
